anomalies.observed: On the DISPLAY sheet (display.kicad_sch, page 5) the interface-strap pins are tied to the opposite rails from the intended I2C configuration: the VCC arrow (top right) is connected to BS0 (pin 10) and BS2 (pin 12), while the GND symbol is connected to BS1 (pin 11), i.e. BS2,BS1,BS0 = 1,0,1.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the SSD1306 must be strapped for I2C: 'BS0 (pin 10) → GND, BS1 (pin 11) → VCC, BS2 (pin 12) → GND. That BS2,BS1,BS0 = 0,1,0 strapping ... is the SSD1306's documented I2C-mode pin configuration'. The data lines are in fact wired for I2C (D0→DISP_SCL/NET0017, D1+D2→DISP_SDA/NET0019 with pull-ups), so the straps must be 0,1,0 to match.

evidence.quote: BS0 (pin 10) → GND; BS1 (pin 11) → VCC; BS2 (pin 12) → GND. That BS2,BS1,BS0 = 0,1,0 strapping, together with D0→DISP_SCL and D1+D2 tied together →DISP_SDA, is the SSD1306's documented I2C-mode pin configuration
display.kicad_sch (page 5): VCC arrow at top right joins the BS0 and BS2 horizontal wires; GND symbol joins the BS1 wire

anomalies.impact: The SSD1306 is not placed in I2C mode, so the MCU's I2C-style SCL/SDA lines on D0/D1/D2 are not interpreted as an I2C bus; the OLED will not respond and the display subsystem is non-functional, contradicting the intended architecture.

parsed.summary: The display's SSD1306 interface-strap pins (BS0/BS1/BS2) are tied to the wrong rails (1,0,1 instead of the spec-mandated 0,1,0 I2C strapping), which is inconsistent with the I2C wiring on D0/D1/D2 and would leave the OLED unusable; reference-designator renumbering across the build is a non-electrical artifact and is not reported.
